subject: Clarify: private deployment — customer keys, operator access, and subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@meditechhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditechhealth.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@meditechhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Clarification: private deployment — BYOK isolation and subprocessor routing

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our security team reviewed the private deployment materials and had a few follow-ups before we can move to legal redlines:

- BYOK custody: we need an explicit statement that customer-managed keys (HSM or KMS) remain under Meditech control and that Redwood personnel will not have routine access to plaintext keys. If there are emergency breakglass procedures that require operator intervention, we need the mechanics and required approvals spelled out.
- Operator/network access: confirm which agent/operator accounts (if any) can access VMs or nodes in the private VPC/on-prem installation, and whether those accounts may ever access decrypted model inputs/outputs.
- Subprocessor routing & telemetry: our DPO wants assurance telemetry (logs/metrics) will not leave our selected region except where legally necessary; any subprocessor that receives telemetry must be listed in the DPA annex or pre-approved.
- Evidence: please provide a simple network zone diagram and an annotated DPA redline we can circulate internally.

Can you send a short mutual action plan and the artifacts above? We’d like to have legal review the redline by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Alex Porter
Head of IT Security
Meditech Health

(attachments: none in this message)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@meditechhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarification: private deployment — BYOK isolation and subprocessor routing

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can accommodate all of these; below are the high-level answers and proposed next steps. I’ll attach a short one-pager and an initial redline for your legal team.

Quick answers:
- BYOK custody: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via external HSMs or customer KMS. Keys used to unwrap per-tenant key material are controlled by you; Redwood’s operator processes never persist plaintext customer keys. We will provide a DPA addendum clause committing to "no routine operator plaintext access."
- Breakglass: emergency operator actions are possible only via a documented breakglass flow that requires two authorized approvers (customer SSO + Redwood security approver) and is fully logged. Breakglass events produce immutable audit records and we will provide post-event forensics package on request.
- Operator/network access: Operator accounts are limited to control-plane endpoints in a separate management network segment; they do not have access to customer storage volumes containing decrypted inference inputs/outputs. In on‑prem installs we recommend a bastion jump-host controlled by the customer; for VPCs we can run operator tooling in a dedicated management subnet with strict security group rules.
- Subprocessors & telemetry: by default telemetry is collected at a minimal level (service health and aggregator metrics). We can scope telemetry forwarding to specific endpoints and refuse cross-border export except under a written exception. We’ll include a subprocessor annex that enumerates any subprocessors that may receive aggregated telemetry and provide a mechanism for you to pre-approve additional subprocessors.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll upload an annotated DPA redline and a simple network zone diagram (attached).
2) Schedule a 30-min technical call next week to walk through the breakglass flow and the proposed network segmentation. Please suggest 2 windows that work for you.
3) If the redline looks good, we’ll deliver a final DPA addendum and a DocuSign link for signatures.

Attached: redwood-privdep-byok-summary.pdf

Would 10–11am ET Tuesday work for a quick call?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(attached: redwood-privdep-byok-summary.pdf)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: proposed language and operational guardrails for Meditech

Rachel / Sean — quick internal note before we send the redline to Meditech. Key items I recommend we offer now to keep negotiation tight and auditable: 

1) No routine plaintext access clause — we commit to no routine read of customer key material. 
2) Breakglass carveout — limited to documented emergency scenarios; require dual authorization (customer IAM approval + Redwood security on-call) and automatic creation of a forensics bundle delivered within 72 hours.
3) Subprocessor routing — offer to list current subprocessors in the DPA annex and provide a 30-day notice for any additions; for telemetry forwarding outside the US, require explicit customer opt-in per region.
4) Network segmentation guidance — propose template security group rules and recommend customer-managed bastion for on‑prem or a customer-owned jump host in VPC.
5) Technical proof points — include a diagram and a short runbook that shows key wrapping: customer CMK wraps per-tenant envelope keys; Redwood stores only wrapped keys. 

I’ll draft the suggested redline language for 1–3 above and leave the exact breakglass SLAs flexible — propose 72h for full forensics delivery with an option to accelerate for critical incidents.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Security & Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@meditechhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meditechhealth.com>, Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditechhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarification: private deployment — BYOK isolation and subprocessor routing

Alex — thanks, and appreciate the fast review. We’ve attached an annotated redline and a network-zone diagram that reflect the language Kimberly and I discussed. Highlights below (quoting your ask and our proposal):

> "we need an explicit statement that customer-managed keys remain under Meditech control and that Redwood personnel will not have routine access to plaintext keys."

We propose the following DPA clause: "Redwood shall not access, use, or persist customer plaintext key material in routine operations. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) will be used to unwrap per-tenant envelope keys; Redwood will only persist wrapped envelope keys. Exception: emergency breakglass events as described below."

> "If there are emergency breakglass procedures that require operator intervention, we need the mechanics and required approvals spelled out."

Breakglass flow (summary):
- Trigger: customer SSO + Customer Security Officer approval OR documented on-call escalation with customer-specified emergency token.
- Redwood action: limited operator action by named on-call engineer; all console activity streamed to immutable audit logs; full forensics package delivered to customer within 72 hours.
- Gov: breakglass events are recorded in a tamper-evident log; customer may request independent audit of that log under the DPA.

> "confirm which agent/operator accounts can access VMs or nodes... and whether those accounts may ever access decrypted model inputs/outputs."

Answer: operator accounts are control-plane only and operate in a separate management subnet. They do not access customer storage volumes that hold decrypted inference inputs/outputs. For on‑prem installs we recommend a customer-managed bastion/jump host; for VPC installs we run Redwood tooling in a non-data plane subnet with no direct access to decrypted S3- or block-storage contents.

> "our DPO wants assurance telemetry will not leave our selected region... any subprocessor that receives telemetry must be listed in the DPA annex or pre-approved."

Answer: we will include a subprocessor annex enumerating subprocessors that may receive aggregated telemetry. We will not export telemetry outside of your chosen region without written consent. We’ll also offer a telemetry minimization profile for Meditech that restricts forwarded metrics to health-only signals unless you authorize additional flows.

Attachments: Meditech_DPA_v3_redline.docx, network_zones_diagram.png

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Meditech legal to review redline (target: Wed 18 Nov).
2) Technical deep-dive with our infra/security team (30–45 mins) — proposed Tue 17 Nov 10am ET.
3) Agree final DPA addendum and sign via DocuSign.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/recipient/1234abcd
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

If that timeline works I’ll set the Tech call and loop in our infra lead.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(attachments: Meditech_DPA_v3_redline.docx, network_zones_diagram.png)
